notes: One tool-using turn on the `hermes chat` REPL whose SECOND API call is 429'd by a mock primary, so Hermes' turn-scoped fallback_providers chain activates and a DIFFERENT model finishes the same turn. Hermes writes no transcript file — the daemon observes $HERMES_HOME/state.db (ProcessOwnedStore); the sessions row is INSERTed only on the first user message, so session_birth is anchored to recording start and left UNPINNED (the transient proc-<PID> pre-session carries the ready birth) and turn1_done chains off turn1_start, the same shape as the basic-turn sibling. KNOWN FAILING (daemon=bug): the load-bearing assertion is that the recorded model is the FALLBACK model id. Today `querySessionMetrics` reads ModelName from `sessions.model`, and Hermes freezes that column after the first accounted API call (the first_accounted_route guard in hermes_state.update_token_counts — 'one row cannot represent mixed-provider usage'), while the fallback route is written to a `session_model_usage` row the adapter never reads. So the recording is EXPECTED to show the primary model id; that mismatch is the bug signature, not a reason to weaken this spec. `record` pins observations.model to the FALLBACK model id from the recipe's config.yaml once that config exists — it is deliberately left unpinned here rather than guessed, and cost is asserted non-zero only if the fallback model prices. The 'no flicker to ready' criterion is only partly machine-checkable: the phase DSL has no bounded mid-turn window that is safe against turn duration, so turn1_start asserts `no state_transition to waiting` (Hermes auto-executes tools) and the ready-flicker check stays a recipe verify item — the failover path appends no message and writes no finish_reason, so no activity event can fire during it.

text: A hermes session appears in ready shortly after launch (the store row does not exist until the first user message, so this is the transient proc-<PID> pre-session — left UNPINNED so it cannot steal identity)
A PID is bound to the session (Hermes is a Python console script, matched on the full command line)

The user prompt drives the store-backed session ready → working; the turn never gates on a permission ask (Hermes auto-executes its tools), so it never enters waiting — including across the provider failover

The SAME session settles back to ready once the FALLBACK model closes the turn (assistant row with finish_reason='stop' → turn_done). No new session is minted: a failover swaps the backend, never the session
